note: Canonical Drug of the Day series queue. 70 entries across the psychopharmacology + street-drug universe; each with real receptor pharmacology, ChEMBL-sourced affinities, RCSB-verified 3D structures (co-crystal where one exists, honestly labeled surrogate otherwise), harm reduction, and FlexAIDdS entropy-collapse commentary.

series.blurb: Active metabolite of psilocybin. Potent 5-HT2A partial agonist with Gq-biased signalling — the pharmacological reason mushrooms outlast smoked DMT. Dephosphorylation gate: psilocybin is a prodrug; psilocin is the ligand that actually binds.

Lysergic acid diethylamide — the ergoline scaffold with a diethylamide 'lid' that traps the ligand in the receptor binding pocket, explaining the 8–12 h duration despite sub-nanomolar affinity. 5-HT2B cardiac liability meets 5-HT2A psychedelic efficacy.

The reference monoamine releaser. DAT/NET substrate that reverses transporter flux — pharmacological parent of MDMA, methamphetamine, and the entire ADHD stimulant class. CYP2D6 hydroxylation to p-hydroxyamphetamine; trace amine-associated receptor 1 (TAAR1) negative feedback.

N-phenyl-N-[1-(2-phenylethyl)piperidin-4-yl]propanamide — sub-nanomolar MOR agonist with extreme lipophilicity (log P ~4). Rapid CNS penetration, narrow therapeutic index, and the structural reason illicit analogs (carfentanil, acetylfentanyl) are lethal at microgram doses. Naloxone-reversible; test your supply.

Editorial pick: breaks the tryptamine arc. The only common hallucinogen with zero meaningful 5-HT2A activity — a neoclerodane diterpene and selective κ-opioid full agonist. Dissociative-adjacent phenomenology from KOR signalling in claustrum and ACC, not serotonin. Proof that 'psychedelic' is a phenomenology, not a receptor class.

The reference opioid every other is measured against. Full μ-opioid agonist, Gi/o-coupled, naloxone-reversible. MOR Ki ~1.8 nM (ChEMBL, human OPRM1). Structure shown is the active-state μ-opioid receptor with agonist BU72 (PDB 5C1M) — no morphine co-crystal exists. Active metabolite M6G; respiratory depression is the killer, and it is fatally synergistic with benzodiazepines and alcohol.

Monoamine substrate-releaser: rides DAT/NET/SERT inward and reverses flux. DAT dopamine-release EC50 ~24.5 nM, NET ~12.3 nM (Rothman 2001); TAAR1 agonist as a negative-feedback brake. PDB 4XP6 is a genuine methamphetamine co-crystal in the Drosophila DAT S1 site — the closest crystallized homolog of human DAT. Hyperthermia, cardiovascular strain, and sleep-deprivation psychosis are the real risks; test for fentanyl adulteration.

Dissociative anesthetic and rapid antidepressant. Use-dependent open-channel blocker of the NMDA receptor (PCP-site Ki ~420 nM, ChEMBL); disinhibition drives an AMPA/BDNF/mTOR plasticity cascade behind the esketamine antidepressant effect. PDB 7EU7 is the S-ketamine-bound human NMDAR cryo-EM structure. Watch ulcerative cystitis (K-bladder), dissociation injury, and the redose trap; fatal with other depressants.

The reason cannabis is not 'spice'. Δ9-THC is a low-efficacy CB1 partial agonist (CB1 Ki ~40 nM, ChEMBL), which is exactly why it has a ceiling that synthetic full agonists lack. CYP2C9/3A4 metabolism yields active 11-OH-THC. PDB 5XRA is human CB1 with the THC-derived agonist AM11542 in the same pocket. Real risks: cannabinoid hyperemesis, anxiety/tachycardia, impaired driving.

The most-used psychoactive on Earth, and the least understood. α4β2 nAChR agonist (high-affinity-state Ki ~1 nM, ChEMBL); desensitization and receptor upregulation drive dependence via VTA dopamine, with a habenular α5 aversion brake. PDB 5KXI is human α4β2 with nicotine bound (ligand NCT). The combustion is the killer, not the alkaloid — NRT and vaping sit far lower on the risk curve.

Stimulation by disinhibition: caffeine antagonizes adenosine A2A/A1 receptors (A2A Ki ~2.4 µM, ChEMBL), lifting the brake on dopamine and arousal rather than pushing the accelerator. CYP1A2 converts it to paraxanthine. PDB 5MZP is a genuine caffeine co-crystal at A2A (ligand CFF). Tolerance and withdrawal are real; the acute danger is anhydrous caffeine powder, where a teaspoon can be lethal.

The archetypal benzodiazepine. Positive allosteric modulator at the GABA-A α/γ interface — raises Cl⁻ channel opening frequency (Ki ~14 nM, ChEMBL), does nothing without GABA present. Long-acting active metabolites (nordazepam, oxazepam, temazepam) via CYP2C19/3A4. PDB 6HUP is diazepam-bound human α1β3γ2 GABA-A. Fatally synergistic with opioids and alcohol; abrupt cessation risks seizures — taper, never stop cold.

The phenethylamine psychedelic that predates the tryptamine canon. 5-HT2A agonist ~500x weaker than LSD (5-HT2A Ki ~551 nM, ChEMBL) — which is precisely why oral doses run 200–400 mg and the trip lasts 10–12 h. PDB 7RAN is an active-state 5-HT2A–mini-Gq complex (no mescaline co-crystal exists). Long, nausea-heavy, and a hard contraindication with MAOIs.

series.tagline: The prodrug that outran the law
series.blurb: Diacetylmorphine is a lipophilic prodrug: it crosses the BBB fast, then deacetylates to 6-MAM and morphine (MOR Ki ~1.8 nM, ChEMBL). Structure is active-state MOR + BU72 (PDB 5C1M) — no heroin co-crystal. The lethal reality now is fentanyl adulteration; naloxone reverses it, and it is fatally synergistic with benzodiazepines and alcohol.

series.tagline: The pill that lit the crisis
series.blurb: Full µ-opioid agonist (MOR Ki ~12 nM, ChEMBL); CYP2D6 yields the more potent oxymorphone. Active-state MOR + BU72 shown (PDB 5C1M) — no oxycodone co-crystal. The OxyContin reformulation pushed users toward heroin/fentanyl. Respiratory depression, naloxone-reversible, fatal with benzos/alcohol.

Full µ agonist (MOR Ki ~13 nM, ChEMBL) with NMDA antagonism (~3–8 µM). Active-state MOR + BU72 shown (PDB 5C1M). The 15–60 h variable half-life makes it a maintenance workhorse and an accumulation hazard; QT prolongation → torsades. Long duration outlasts naloxone; fatal with benzos/alcohol.

Ultra-high MOR affinity (Ki ~0.2 nM, ChEMBL), slow dissociation, partial agonism → a respiratory-depression ceiling that makes it a safer maintenance agent. Active-state MOR + BU72 shown (PDB 5C1M) — no buprenorphine co-crystal. Precipitated withdrawal if dosed too early; still fatal with benzos/alcohol.

series.tagline: Opioid by metabolite, SNRI by design
series.blurb: Parent is a weak µ agonist (MOR Ki ~1600 nM); CYP2D6 makes O-desmethyltramadol (M1, ~3.4 nM) — so effect swings with metabolizer status. Also inhibits SERT/NET. Active-state MOR + BU72 shown (PDB 5C1M). Seizure risk, serotonin syndrome with SSRIs/MAOIs, respiratory depression in ultrarapid metabolizers.

The primary kratom alkaloid: G-protein-biased µ partial agonist (MOR Ki ~7.2 nM, ChEMBL) with little β-arrestin recruitment — mechanistically why respiratory risk runs lower than classical opioids. PDB 7T2G is a genuine MOR–Gi + mitragynine-pseudoindoxyl cryo-EM. Metabolite 7-OH is more potent; real dependence and adulteration risk remain.

A pure DAT/NET reuptake blocker (DAT Ki ~34 nM, ChEMBL) — the mechanistic opposite of amphetamine's efflux. d-threo is the eutomer; CES1 hydrolyzes it to ritalinic acid. dDAT + cocaine shown as the S1-blocker surrogate (PDB 4XP4) — no methylphenidate co-crystal. Cardiovascular risk; insufflation/IV diversion adds talc-lung harm.

A DAT/NET-selective reuptake blocker up to ~50x more potent than cocaine (DAT IC50 ~2.1 nM, ChEMBL) and a pure blocker, not a releaser. dDAT + dopamine shown for the S1 pocket (PDB 4XP1) — no MDPV co-crystal. Extreme potency + long duration drive compulsive redosing, hyperthermia, and agitated delirium; test kits matter.

Non-selective monoamine releaser with an MDMA-like DA:5-HT balance (DAT release EC50 ~49 nM, SERT ~118 nM, ChEMBL/Simmler). dDAT + methamphetamine shown as the releaser surrogate (PDB 4XP6) — no mephedrone co-crystal. Short euphoria drives compulsive redosing and vasoconstriction; the UK ban outran the pharmacology.

A 4-bromo phenethylamine and Shulgin classic: 5-HT2A partial agonist (Ki ~34 nM antagonist-state / low-nM agonist-state, ChEMBL). Active-state 5-HT2A–Gq shown (PDB 7RAN) — no 2C-B co-crystal. Steep dose-response (a few mg matters), frequently mis-sold; contraindicated with MAOIs.

The N-benzyl on 2C-I turns a moderate psychedelic into a sub-nanomolar 5-HT2A agonist (Ki ~2.2 nM, ChEMBL). PDB 6WHA is 5-HT2A + the close NBOH-class analog 25CN-NBOH. Sold on blotter as 'LSD' but far more dangerous: vasoconstriction, seizures, hyperthermia, deaths. Test kits distinguish it from LSD — use them.

Shulgin's 'STP': the α-methyl blocks MAO, stretching duration to 14–20 h — which caused the 1967 overdose scare when users redosed a slow-onset drug. Potent 5-HT2A partial agonist (Ki low-nM to hundreds nM across assays, PDSP/ChEMBL). PDB 6WHA is 5-HT2A + 25CN-NBOH. Slow onset + long tail = the stacking trap; MAOI contraindication.

Inactive until alkaline phosphatase strips the phosphate to give psilocin (the #004 payload; psilocin 5-HT2A Ki ~107 nM vs psilocybin >10 µM, ChEMBL). PDB 7WC5 is 5-HT2A + psilocin — the active species. FDA Breakthrough Therapy for depression; psychological safety, set/setting, MAOI caution.

Unlike DMT, 5-MeO-DMT is 5-HT1A-dominant (Ki ~28 nM, ChEMBL) — an intense, short, near-egoless 'release.' PDB 7E2Y is the active 5-HT1A–Gi complex (serotonin-bound; no 5-MeO-DMT co-crystal). O-demethylated to bufotenin; MAO-metabolized. FATAL serotonin toxicity with MAOIs/harmalas. Sonoran toad conservation matters.

Promiscuous: allosteric SERT inhibitor (IC50 ~0.59 µM, ChEMBL) plus NMDA, κ-opioid and sigma activity; active metabolite noribogaine. PDB 6DZV is a genuine SERT–ibogaine cryo-EM complex. Real promise interrupting opioid withdrawal — and genuine danger: hERG/QT prolongation → torsades → sudden death. Requires cardiac monitoring; deadly with QT drugs and post-dose opioids.

Phencyclidine names the NMDA 'PCP site': a use-dependent open-channel blocker ~15–20x more potent than ketamine (Ki ~23 nM, ChEMBL) with longer channel residence. PDB 7SAB is a genuine PCP-bound GluN1/GluN2B NMDAR (ligand 1PC). Also hits DAT and sigma. Unpredictable agitation/analgesia, hyperthermia; don't stack with depressants.
High-potency, short-half-life benzodiazepine — potent panic relief, steep interdose withdrawal and strong dependence. Fatal with opioids/alcohol; taper, never stop cold.
Long-half-life benzodiazepine (anticonvulsant, panic). Same GABA-A BZD-site PAM mechanism as diazepam; smoother curve than alprazolam but the same dependence and depressant-synergy danger.

series.tagline: Not a benzo, acts like one
series.blurb: α1-selective GABA-A modulator — hypnotic with less anxiolytic action, but real complex-sleep behaviours (sleep-driving), next-day impairment and rebound. Fatal with other depressants.

Low-affinity, many-site depressant: potentiates GABA-A, blocks NMDA, hits glycine/nAChR/GIRK. No pocket co-crystal — it acts at diffuse sites. Zero-order kinetics; kindling withdrawal → delirium tremens; fatal with opioids/benzos.

series.tagline: Therapeutic dose to coma in one step
series.blurb: Endogenous metabolite and narcolepsy drug with a brutally steep dose-response — recreational to unconscious over a narrow range. GABA-B + high-affinity GHB site. Severe benzo/baclofen-refractory withdrawal; fatal with alcohol/depressants.

A baclofen/gabapentinoid hybrid sold as a supplement: GABA-B agonist plus α2δ calcium-channel binding. Anxiolytic/nootropic, but dose creep, strong tolerance and a genuinely severe withdrawal syndrome. Don't stack with depressants.

series.tagline: Duration, not frequency — and no ceiling
series.blurb: The classic barbiturate: increases GABA-A channel OPEN DURATION and directly gates at high dose — so unlike benzos there is no overdose ceiling. Potent CYP inducer, withdrawal seizures; fatal with opioids/alcohol.

series.tagline: Not a GABA drug, despite the name
series.blurb: Binds the α2δ-1 auxiliary subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels — reducing excitatory transmitter release. NOT a GABA-receptor ligand. Neuropathic pain/anxiety use, but euphoria and misuse (esp. with opioids raises overdose risk); dependence and withdrawal.

Cough-syrup morphinan that becomes a dissociative at plateau doses via NMDA open-channel block (+ sigma-1). CYP2D6 → dextrorphan. Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs/MAOIs; the real danger is combination products (acetaminophen/antihistamines).

Laughing gas: an NMDA-antagonist anesthetic with seconds-long duration and no defined orthosteric site (shown on NMDAR, honestly labeled). The real harm is chronic use — irreversible B12 inactivation → neuropathy/SACD — and hypoxia; always mix with oxygen.

The therapeutic dissociative: low-affinity, fast-off, strongly voltage-dependent NMDA open-channel block — it filters pathological tonic Ca influx while sparing phasic synaptic signalling. That kinetic difference is why it treats Alzheimer's while ketamine/PCP dissociate.

Prozac: SERT reuptake inhibitor with a weeks-long washout via active norfluoxetine — so low discontinuation syndrome. CYP2D6 inhibitor, activating. Serotonin syndrome is the hard line: fatal with MAOIs.

series.tagline: The SSRI with a DAT streak
series.blurb: Zoloft: sub-nanomolar SERT block with an unusual (for an SSRI) DAT affinity. First-line, relatively pregnancy-safe; GI-heavy. Serotonin syndrome with MAOIs; QT at high dose. Real sertraline co-crystal (6AWO).
The (S)-enantiomer of citalopram and the most SERT-selective SSRI, occupying both the orthosteric S1 and allosteric S2 sites (real co-crystal 5I73). Dose-capped for QT. Serotonin syndrome with MAOIs.

Paxil: the most potent SSRI at SERT, with anticholinergic action and strong self-CYP2D6 inhibition (nonlinear kinetics). Short half-life + potency = the worst discontinuation syndrome. Real paroxetine co-crystal (5I6X).

Effexor: dose-dependent SNRI — serotonergic low, noradrenergic added higher. Notorious short-half-life discontinuation ('brain zaps'), dose-dependent hypertension, higher overdose toxicity than SSRIs. Serotonin syndrome with MAOIs.

Wellbutrin/Zyban: dopamine/noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (workhorse metabolite hydroxybupropion) plus nicotinic antagonism for smoking cessation. Weight-neutral, activating, no sexual dysfunction — but dose-dependent seizure risk (contraindicated in eating disorders).

series.tagline: The one that kills in overdose
series.blurb: A tricyclic: SERT/NET reuptake block plus potent H1, muscarinic, α1 and cardiac Na-channel blockade. Low-dose for pain/migraine/sleep. Narrow therapeutic index — overdose is lethal via QRS-widening Na-channel block (bicarbonate antidote). Fatal with MAOIs.

Irreversible non-selective MAOI (hydrazine) — a ~2-week washout to resynthesize enzyme. The tyramine 'cheese reaction' → hypertensive crisis, and serotonin syndrome with any serotonergic. The most interaction-dangerous antidepressant.

The archetypal typical antipsychotic: high-affinity D2 antagonist (real haloperidol co-crystal 6LUQ). Potent D2 blockade → strong EPS/tardive dyskinesia, hyperprolactinemia, NMS and QT. Not a PRN sedative.

series.tagline: The atypical ratio, on a real crystal
series.blurb: Atypical by its 5-HT2A>D2 ratio (real D2–risperidone co-crystal 6CM4). Loses atypicality — gains EPS — at higher dose; potent hyperprolactinemia; active metabolite paliperidone. Metabolic and orthostatic effects; NMS.

Broad multi-receptor antipsychotic (D2/5-HT2A/H1/M/5-HT2C). Effective, but the worst metabolic syndrome — H1/5-HT2C-driven weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia. Sedating; NMS; the IM olanzapine+benzodiazepine warning.

Seroquel: loose, fast-dissociating D2 antagonist with very high H1 affinity; metabolite norquetiapine adds NET inhibition. Dose-tiered — low = sedative, mid = antidepressant, high = antipsychotic. Massively over-prescribed off-label for sleep. Metabolic, orthostasis, QT.

The 'dopamine stabilizer': D2 PARTIAL agonist (+ 5-HT2A antagonist, 5-HT1A partial agonist), so lower EPS/prolactin — but can destabilize if switched from an antagonist. Long half-life, akathisia signature, and the impulse-control (gambling/hypersexuality) warning.

Uniquely effective in treatment-resistant schizophrenia via a promiscuous profile (D4>D2 low-occupancy, 5-HT2A, muscarinic, H1). Last-line because of agranulocytosis (mandatory ANC monitoring), myocarditis, seizures, and fatal ileus. Never miss bloodwork.

A monovalent cation, not a receptor drug: inhibits GSK-3β and inositol monophosphatase by displacing catalytic Mg²⁺ (shown on GSK-3β; Li⁺ isn't an organic ligand). Gold-standard anti-suicidal efficacy but a narrow therapeutic index — NSAIDs/thiazides/ACE and dehydration push it toxic.

Phenyltriazine that stabilizes the inactivated state of voltage-gated Na channels → less glutamate release (real lamotrigine–Nav1.7 co-crystal 8THH). Best for bipolar depression. Mandatory slow titration: too fast, or combined with valproate, risks Stevens-Johnson/TEN.

Non-intoxicating because it is NOT a CB1 agonist — it's a negative allosteric modulator, plus 5-HT1A/TRPV1/GPR55 activity. Epidiolex (epilepsy) is FDA-approved. Main real risk is CYP-mediated drug interactions and unregulated-product purity.

The original 'Spice/K2' cannabinoid and the mechanistic reason it's dangerous: a CB1 FULL agonist with no ceiling (unlike THC's partial agonism), so seizures, psychosis, tachyarrhythmia, AKI and deaths. Uneven spraying = no safe dose. 'It's just fake weed' is lethal.

The endogenous cannabinoid ('ananda' = bliss): an on-demand retrograde CB1 partial agonist, rapidly destroyed by FAAH (why it's fleeting, and why FAAH inhibitors are a drug class). Linked to runner's high. An educational endogenous-ligand entry.

The active principle of Amanita muscaria: a potent DIRECT (orthosteric) GABA-A agonist — unlike benzodiazepine modulators. Formed from ibotenic acid on drying. Sedative/oneiric, non-serotonergic; harm is ibotenic delirium, dose variability and deadly Amanita mis-ID.

The β-carboline that makes oral DMT work: a reversible MAO-A inhibitor (real MAO-A–harmine co-crystal 2Z5X) plus DYRK1A inhibition. Reversibility is safer than irreversible MAOIs but still creates the MAOI danger set — serotonin syndrome with SSRIs is the real ayahuasca risk.

An α2-adrenergic antagonist — blocking the autoreceptor brake raises noradrenergic outflow. Historically an aphrodisiac, now a fat-loss supplement and an anxiety/panic research probe. Hypertension, tachycardia, panic; dangerous with stimulants and MAOIs.

A non-selective muscarinic antagonist and genuine deliriant (Datura/'Devil's Breath') — dysphoric, amnestic, nothing like a recreational trip. Medical use as a motion-sickness patch. Overdose is the anticholinergic toxidrome; Datura dosing is lethal-unpredictable (physostigmine antidote).

A sedating H1 antihistamine that at high dose becomes an antimuscarinic deliriant and a cardiac Na-channel blocker. The 'high' is miserable and dangerous (hat-man hallucinations). Overdose = anticholinergic toxidrome + seizures + QRS-widening cardiotoxicity; the 'Benadryl challenge' has killed.

Chantix: an α4β2 nicotinic PARTIAL agonist (real varenicline–α4β2 co-crystal 6UR8) — enough dopamine to blunt craving while blocking nicotine's full reward. Best-in-class cessation efficacy; nausea and vivid dreams; the neuropsychiatric warning was later de-escalated (EAGLES).

A non-sedating, non-dependent anxiolytic: 5-HT1A partial agonist (+ D2 antagonism) unlike benzodiazepines. Weeks to work, no abuse liability, no benzo cross-tolerance (so it can't cover benzo withdrawal). GAD and SSRI augmentation; serotonin syndrome with MAOIs; grapefruit/CYP3A4.

The long-acting antagonist cousin of naloxone: blocks µ-opioid reward (and via endogenous-opioid blockade, treats alcohol use disorder too). Must be opioid-free to start (precipitated withdrawal). Lost tolerance means overdose risk if someone relapses after a depot wanes.
